clue.text: Make mistake — almost get fired

indicators.note: almost means the phrase is not quite complete, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a gun or firework that is fired is said to go off

explanation.surface: Someone nearly loses their job over an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get fired' reads as being sacked, but it is GO OFF, as a gun does.
explanation.definitionFit: To goof is an informal verb for blundering or slipping up.

clue.text: Something left on account: variable amount

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown or variable quantities

explanation.surface: A bookkeeping note about a variable sum carried on an account.
explanation.walkthrough: ON = LEG is the cricket convention: the leg side of the field is also the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy is property or money bequeathed in a will, something left behind by the deceased.

clue.text: Leader once exceptionally busy in launderette?

wordplay.note: a launderette working flat out might be washing a ton of clothes

explanation.surface: A former leader is seen frantically doing laundry.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as WASHING TON: shifting a ton of washing is what a very busy launderette does.
explanation.definitionFit: George Washington was the first President of the United States, a national leader of the past.

clue.text: Extortionist confident in ancient city

indicators.note: the word for confident sits within the name of the old city

parts.note: Ur was a city of ancient Mesopotamia, a crossword favourite
sure means certain or confident

explanation.surface: A self-assured extortioner operates in some city of antiquity.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer lends money at exorbitant interest, extorting excessive repayment from borrowers.

clue.text: Criminal blame attaches to last character on display

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are corrupted, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
Z is the final letter of the alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: Blame for a crime is pinned on the final person seen on show.
explanation.definitionFit: To emblazon is to display prominently, originally a heraldic device on a shield.

clue.text: Nimble ace ejected from jet

indicators.note: the letter for ace is thrown out of the word for jet

parts.note: a jet of liquid is a spray

explanation.surface: An agile fighter pilot bails out of an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jet' and 'ace' paint an aerial dogfight, but the jet is a jet of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry describes someone, often older, who is still lively and active on their feet.

clue.text: Attendant in uniform entering my bank

indicators.note: the letter for uniform goes into the exclamation for my

parts.note: cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a bank of seats is a tier, a row above another

explanation.surface: A uniformed attendant walks into the narrator's bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is not a possessive here but an exclamation, as is COR, a British cry of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtier is someone who attends a royal court as a companion or adviser to the monarch.

clue.text: Scots head meets the Spanish composer in city

parts.note: heid is the Scots form of head
el is the Spanish for the
Alban Berg was an Austrian composer

explanation.surface: A Scottish leader meets a Spanish composer in some city.
explanation.definitionFit: Heidelberg is a German university city on the river Neckar.

clue.text: Longer and shorter periods reversed in Greek letter

indicators.note: the two time words together are read backwards

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
a mo is a moment, a short time

explanation.surface: Time spans long and short get flipped inside a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last of the twenty-four letters of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Signalling English plan to invade beach

indicators.note: the letters for English and plan go into the word for beach as invaders would land

parts.note: a beach is the shore
a map is a plan of an area

explanation.surface: A military signal about an English plan to land on a beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Semaphore is a system of signalling with hand-held flags held in set positions.

clue.text: Energy in pop one among things that get us down?

definitions.text: one among things that get us down?

indicators.note: the letter for energy sits inside the word for pop

parts.note: pop is an informal name for one's father

explanation.surface: Energy in Dad is one of the things that depresses us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get us down' suggests depression, but down is the soft plumage a bird grows.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is fine soft plumage, so each feather is one of the things that gives birds their down.

clue.text: Like some cakes put before daughter

parts.note: to lay something is to put it down
ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: A baker sets out cakes ahead of the daughter's arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer cake is built from tiers of sponge with filling between, so it is layered.

clue.text: Fabric light with no backing

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light

indicators.note: backing means the word no is turned round

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lightweight fabric with no lining behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' sounds like a lining for the fabric, but it turns the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is a synthetic textile made from regenerated cellulose, used for clothes.

clue.text: Fish on sea bed finds lowest possible level

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece placed on another comes above it

parts.note: rock, or rock salmon, is a fishmonger's name for dogfish
the sea bed is the bottom of the sea

explanation.surface: A fish found on the seabed has reached the lowest point possible.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock salmon, or rock, is a British fish-and-chip-shop name for dogfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock bottom is the idiom for the very lowest point anything can reach.

clue.text: Are we told put up a poster or flyer?

indicators.note: asks whether we heard it, so the answer comes from the sound of the words

parts.note: to put up a poster is to raise a bill, a bill being a printed notice

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they were told to put up a poster or a flyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flyer' looks like another word for a leaflet beside 'poster', but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The razorbill is a black-and-white seabird of the auk family, so it is a flyer.

clue.text: Surprising fact about Victor and Joy

parts.note: re means about or concerning
V is Victor in the NATO phonetic alphabet
elation is great joy

explanation.surface: A startling discovery about a man named Victor and a woman called Joy.
explanation.definitionFit: A revelation is something disclosed that comes as a surprise to people.

clue.text: What may make CV an exact reference?

wordplay.note: C and V can be abbreviations for the two words of the answer joined by and

explanation.surface: Asks what makes a curriculum vitae precise and accurate.
explanation.walkthrough: CV looks like a curriculum vitae, but here it is C and V, the abbreviations used in Bible citations.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapter and verse is an idiom for precise authority or detail, from citing Bible passages.

clue.text: Woman deceived reportedly by a snake

indicators.note: reportedly means the answer comes from how the words are spoken

parts.note: Anna, a woman's name, plus conned, meaning deceived
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman was reportedly fooled by a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The anaconda is a large constricting snake of South American rivers.

clue.text: Laboratory chemicals are working on toilet

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are in action, moved into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the Gents is a British name for a men's public toilet

explanation.surface: Lab chemicals are operating on a lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gents is the usual British sign and name for a men's public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Reagents are substances used in laboratories to bring about or detect chemical reactions.

clue.text: Bright idea: view a barn that's renovated

indicators.note: a renovated building is remodelled, so its letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has a clever plan after seeing a done-up barn.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainwave is a sudden inspiration or clever idea.

clue.text: Shot where force breaches European citadel

indicators.note: the letter for force breaks into the letters for European citadel

parts.note: a fort is a fortified stronghold

explanation.surface: An army breaches the defences of a European citadel with a shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a shot at something means making an attempt, which is an effort.

clue.text: Kelly in Greggs keeps serving up Whoppers!

indicators.note: the run of words keeps the answer held inside them

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of Kelly, the word in and the start of Greggs

explanation.surface: A worker named Kelly at the bakery chain Greggs dishes out burgers.
explanation.walkthrough: Greggs is a British bakery chain; Whoppers suggests Burger King's burger, but means big lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Serving up whoppers means telling outrageous lies, which is lying.

clue.text: What's melting in current century with rising speed?

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: pace means speed

explanation.surface: Something is melting this century, faster and faster.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar ice caps are melting as global temperatures climb.

clue.text: Thrash trespasser's extremities with cat

indicators.note: the extremities of the word are its two end letters

parts.note: only the two end letters of trespasser are used
the ounce is the snow leopard, a big cat

explanation.surface: Beat an intruder's hands and feet with a whip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cat' suggests a cat-o'-nine-tails for thrashing, but it is the snow leopard.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce is to defeat heavily or to beat soundly.

clue.text: Ham he produced, but saved some animals

definitions.text: Ham he produced, but saved some animals

parts.note: in Genesis Ham is one of the three sons of the man who built the ark
the animals went into the ark two by two to escape the Flood

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' looks like meat from a farmer's pigs; it is the Biblical son.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical patriarch fathered Shem, Ham and Japheth and rescued pairs of creatures from the Flood in his ark.

clue.text: Female, Italian head, shows suitability

parts.note: It is short for Italian, as in It vermouth
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Inverness

explanation.surface: A female Italian boss demonstrates she is fit for the role.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitness can mean appropriateness for a purpose, not just physical health.

clue.text: Hands over an item exchanged?

indicators.note: over means the word for hands is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: paws is a jocular word for hands

explanation.surface: Someone hands across an object in a trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands over' looks like a verb phrase for giving, but splits into hands and a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A swap, as a noun, is a thing traded for something else.

clue.text: Art with models posed in work of Michelangelo?

indicators.note: the models are posed, arranged into a new order with the word art

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Artwork featuring posing models in something Michelangelo painted.
explanation.definitionFit: An old master is a painting by a great European artist of the period before about 1800, such as Michelangelo.

clue.text: Zero degrees — one seen at many a summit?

definitions.text: one seen at many a summit

parts.note: O looks like the figure zero
BA and MA, Bachelor and Master of Arts, are two university degrees

explanation.surface: No qualifications needed for someone often at mountain peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summit' suggests a mountain top, but it is a meeting of world leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: Barack Obama, as US President, attended many international summit meetings of world leaders.
